intro.title: Event Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive form component that captures user input. You will learn how to properly type React event handlers, such as those for form submissions and input changes, using TypeScript. The core concept is using TypeScript's generic types like `React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>` to ensure your event handlers are type-safe. This involves working with React's `useState` hook and event handler functions. By the end, you'll understand how TypeScript helps prevent common errors by defining the expected shape of event objects.
intro.usecase: Event typing is essential for building robust interactive UIs in real-world applications. In complex dashboards with multiple filters and controls, proper event typing ensures that search inputs, date pickers, and dropdown selections handle user interactions correctly. When building forms for e-commerce checkout or user registration, typed events prevent bugs by catching invalid event handlers during development. This pattern is also critical in data visualization tools where users interact with charts through clicks, hovers, and drag events, maintaining type safety across all user interactions.
